newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops advance into rebel heartland.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops advance into rebel heartland.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops advanced into areas held by Tamil Tiger rebels on Wednesday after launching a major offensive to open a strategic land route to the northern town of Jaffna, military officials said.
They said the troops were inching along from northern Vavuniya town, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, into the mostly jungle-covered Wanni region.
"The advance is firm but slow as security forces steer their way through mines," one military official in the north said.
He said troops were near Omanthai, north of Vavuniya, but were short of capturing the town.

Other military officials said a column of troops advancing north frOm the Pemmaduwa area, east of Vavuniya, had met resistance from the rebels on Wednesday morning. A few soldiers had been wounded in the battle, they said.
Civilians in Vavuniya said they heard artillery shells being fired at areas held by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) since early on Wednesday.
Troops backed by helicopter gunships, artillery and tanks advanced five km (three miles) into the rebel-held Wanni region, meeting little resistance, the defence ministry said on Tuesday.
"Enemy transmissions indicated four LTTE cadres were killed and a fair number were wounded," it said. There were no troop casualties, it added.

The main aim of the offensive, code-named "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", was to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya and the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north, military officials in the north said.
They said that the navy had also joined the battle and launched a pre-dawn attack on LTTE-held areas on the northeastern coast in Mullaitivu district.

The clandestine Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in Vavuniya, on Wednesday confirmed the naval attacks on Chenmalai and Alampil. It said one fisherman was killed and several others were wounded in the attack.

The radio also said that the Sri Lankan air force had attacked several areas in the Mullaitivu district on Tuesday. Six fishermen were killed and seven wounded in the Mullivaykkal area during bombardment by Kfir jets, it said.
A spokesman for the LTTE's international office in London told Reuters details of the offensive had not yet reached them.
But the rebels said earlier they were prepared to face it.
Last July, government forces advanced further south of Jaffna, moving about 20 km (12 miles) down from the peninsula to Kilinochchi, forcing their way into the rebel heartland.
The current offensive plans to link Kilinochchi with Vavuniya, establishing a military land supply route all the way to Jaffna.
LTTE rebels are fighting a 13-year-old war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict, but the LTTE says the toll is higher.
Military officials in the north said a large number of troops had begun moving out from three places and were most likely heading towards Mankulam, about 40 km (25 miles) north of Vavuniya.
This is the year's second major offensive by government forces. In February, they captured another key land route linking Vavuniya with the town of Mannar in the island's west coast.
